sections.h2: Fastest route to a sale in Seguin
sections.html:
Buyers paying cash for a house in its current state generally close soonest. There is no lender, no appraisal and no repair list to hold things up. Listing with an agent can bring a higher price, yet it means prep work, showings and waiting on a stranger's loan.

Seguin is the Guadalupe County seat, on Interstate 10 and the Guadalupe River, about 35 miles northeast of San Antonio. Local buyers and San Antonio commuters both shop here.

Decide what matters most before you call anyone. A fixed closing date, a clean exit from a troubled house and the highest price each lead to a different kind of sale.

sections.h2: Older homes and what buyers expect
sections.html: Seguin was laid out in 1838 and incorporated in 1853, so the older neighborhoods hold houses with real age, including antebellum homes. Houses that old tend to need roof, wiring or plumbing work, and a buyer will price it in. If you have receipts for updates, put them on the table early.

Guadalupe Appraisal District values property here, and its main office is in Seguin. Its member list includes the City of Seguin and Seguin ISD, the school district most Seguin buyers ask about.

An Appraisal Review Board hears appeals, with a taxpayer liaison officer on site on hearing days. On the district's website you can file for homestead, disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions online, or print the forms.

Who to contact for a Seguin parcel
QuestionWhere to go
Is my value correct?Guadalupe Appraisal District, 830-303-3313
Where do I get an exemption form?Guadalupe Appraisal District online tools or office
When is my bill due?County tax office; due on receipt, delinquent after January 31
Who sets the rate?Each taxing unit, such as the city, school district and county

One tip from the district: take time-sensitive mail to a post office counter for a manual postmark, because automated processing can change the postmark date.

The City of Seguin wants a permit before you build, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, roof, re-roof or fence. No permit is needed for painting, siding, window replacement in an existing single-family home or duplex, fences under seven feet, or roofing above the deck.

An owner can do permitted work personally if the home is registered as a homestead with the Guadalupe appraisal district. Hired work has to go through a contractor registered with the city.

For a one or two family home, the approved final inspection report serves as the certificate of occupancy. No separate paper is issued. Wondering whether a past project was permitted? The permits office at 830-401-2435 can look it up.

sections.h2: Permit portal and why sellers should check it
sections.html:
Permits run through the city's Development Services Portal, where applicants request inspections and contractors register. The Permits Department answers at 830-401-2435, and inspection reports go by email to the contacts on each permit. The same office handles floodplain permits and inspections.

Codes in force include the 2023 National Electric Code, the 2021 plumbing, mechanical, building, energy and property maintenance codes, the 2018 fire code and the Seguin Unified Development Code. Seguin has also adopted a flood ordinance that follows FEMA guidance.

A buyer's inspector will compare what stands on the lot with what was permitted. Pull your permit history, keep the final inspection reports, and ask the office about anything that looks unfinished.

  • No permit: painting, siding, window replacement in an existing single-family home or duplex, fences under seven feet, roofing above the deck.
  • Permit needed: building, enlarging, altering, moving, demolishing or re-roofing.
  • Contact: Permits Department, 830-401-2435.

The January 1 date fixes value, and October brings the bills. Most owners have until January 31, and charges start the following day.

A deed for Guadalupe County land is recorded by the county clerk after a notary or comparable officer witnesses the signing. Ask the clerk what recording costs today.

  • Warranty and quitclaim deeds are filed with the county clerk.
  • A trustee's deed comes after a foreclosure auction.
  • Unpaid tax can attach to the house, and clear title waits until it is paid.
  • A title company can quote a payoff before you sign a contract.

The appraised value of a homestead is capped at 10 percent growth a year, with the cap beginning the year after the owner first qualifies. Owners 65 or older or disabled also get a school tax ceiling fixed at what they paid in the year they qualified.

A disabled veteran may receive a rating based exemption, and the district lists those among its application tools. The general exemption deadline is before May 1. When the seller never held an exemption, a buyer late in the year may ask for it for the months left.

Once February 1 passes with a bill open, it is delinquent and the debt can attach to the house, which holds up clear title. A sale can still go forward. Have the title company quote a payoff before you sign, and the balance is paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the county tax office for the figure in writing, and keep the receipt afterward.

Seguin attracts both investors and families, so offers differ. Ask who orders the title search, who covers recording, whether the buyer will accept the house with its permit history as it stands, and what proof of funds they can show. A buyer who answers in writing gives you something to compare. If an offer assumes repairs, find out whether the price already reflects them. If a work item was done without a permit, say so up front, since the buyer's inspector will notice it anyway.

Paperwork comes first with an inherited house. Texas lets heirs probate a will for up to four years after the death, and an estate owing nothing beyond liens on the land may use a muniment of title. A small estate affidavit may fit a smaller estate with no will, and it needs two disinterested witnesses and court approval.

Tenants can stay through a sale. Emptying the house takes written notice and a justice court filing, and selling with the tenant in place sidesteps both.

A house with deferred repairs is the simplest case. A buyer who takes it as is handles the work, and you skip contractor bids.

sections.h2: What happens at a cash closing
sections.html: After you say yes, the title company starts its file, runs a lien search and asks the tax office what is owed. You then set a closing date and sign before a notary, and the deed goes to the county clerk for recording. Carry photo ID and your deed or estate papers. Look over the settlement statement the day before, and make sure the contract names who pays title and recording fees.

faqs.a: The Guadalupe Appraisal District, whose office is in Seguin. Its member list includes the City of Seguin and Seguin ISD.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for Seguin window replacement?
faqs.a: Not for an existing single-family home or duplex. Roof work above the deck and painting are also exempt, but ask the permits office at 830-401-2435 when in doubt.

faqs.q: Is there a certificate of occupancy for a Seguin house?
faqs.a: For one and two family homes, the approved final inspection report acts as the certificate, and the city issues no separate document.

faqs.q: When must Seguin property tax be paid?
faqs.a: Most owners pay by January 31. A bill unpaid on February 1 is delinquent and begins to accrue charges.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Seguin house that is in probate?
faqs.a: Often yes, once the court has named someone with authority or title moves by muniment or affidavit. Ask a title company which path applies to your estate.
